results.websocket: zig-nostr's own RFC 6455 client (relay.Connection over std.Io.net TCP; std.crypto.tls for wss)
results.crypto: libsecp256k1 0.7.1 (C, bitcoin-core commit 1a53f496, compiled from source by the package)
results.notes: Parsing does not verify (ARCHITECTURE.md); the harness calls nostr.event.verify (recomputes the id with event.computeId, then BIP-340 via keys.Signer) on every delivered event, as the library's README and skill tell apps to. Events whose JSON the parser rejects (the "sig":"" rumors) are skipped by Relay.receive and counted in Relay.unreadable(). One keys.Signer (secp256k1 context) per run, created in setup.

results.websocket: libnostr-z's own RFC 6455 client (src/ws: blocking posix reads, OpenSSL for wss)
results.crypto: libsecp256k1 0.2.0 (C, Ubuntu libsecp256k1-dev, static) via noscrypt 0.1.14 NCVerifyDigest; SHA-256 by StringZilla 4.5.1
results.notes: Relay.receive parses but does not verify; the harness calls Event.validate (id check, then noscrypt NCVerifyDigest; also rejects created_at > now+900 s) on every delivered event, as the noz CLI does. auto_reconnect off; read_timeout_ms (SO_RCVTIMEO, default 60 s) raised to --timeout-ms. Event.validate hashes the RAW JSON text of tags and content as the relay sent it instead of re-serializing the decoded fields, so every valid event whose JSON uses escapes the canonical form does not (\uD83C surrogate pairs, \u2019, \/) fails IdMismatch and is dropped (82 of 994 valid events on smoke): accepted_ok is false. The Event is parsed lazily: content and tag values are never decoded (they are extracted only on access, and nothing accesses them here), and validate() hashes the raw JSON slices, so the row does less parse work than a full-parse client and stays unranked even if the IdMismatch bug is fixed. Relay.receive also parses every message twice with std.json.Value besides the event scanner.

results.websocket: libnostr-z's own RFC 6455 client (src/ws: blocking posix reads, OpenSSL for wss)
results.crypto: libsecp256k1 0.2.0 (C, Ubuntu libsecp256k1-dev, static) via noscrypt 0.1.14 NCVerifyDigest; SHA-256 by StringZilla 4.5.1
results.notes: Variant: fetch-all API. A reader thread per relay (the library's own) parses each event for dedup and queues the raw message; queryParallel parses it again into an Event and returns the list after EOSE; the harness then calls Event.validate on each (inside the timed part), so it shares libnostr-z-relay's IdMismatch on escaped JSON. The Event is parsed lazily: content and tag values are never decoded (they are extracted only on access, and nothing accesses them here), and validate() hashes the raw JSON slices, so the row does less parse work than a full-parse client and stays unranked even if the IdMismatch bug is fixed. PoolOptions.queue_size raised from 10000 to the workload size (a full queue silently drops its oldest message). Setup sets a 200 ms SO_RCVTIMEO on the pool's socket (RelayHandle.client.setReadTimeout, public API): with the default (none) the reader thread stays blocked in read() once the relay is quiet after EOSE, and queryParallel (stopReceiving) and Pool.deinit join it forever. The consumer side polls the queue with 1 ms sleeps.
